measured.title: Requests: the page asks for nothing from another site
measured.note: Every request is written down and stopped, and the page also counts when its markup or style sheets name another site. A place at the page’s own address (a font file at /fonts/, a style sheet, a form action) is not a deviation; it is listed as not shipped with the page.
measured.informationHead: Not shipped with the page. The page names these places at its own address; a page of one file cannot ship them, so a person must supply them or check that they exist. They are not deviations.

measured.title: Colors: every color that the page draws is a color of the Vision
measured.note: A color is a deviation when it is not one of the Vision's opaque colors. Pseudo-elements, outlines, text strokes, and the fill and stroke of inline SVG shapes are compared too. Partly transparent colors are listed as information and not compared.
measured.informationHead: Listed for information and not compared: partly transparent colors. A person must judge them on the page.

measured.title: Typefaces: every text names a typeface of the Vision
measured.note: The first family that each text names is compared; a fallback after it is not. The site’s font files are not there during the check, so the program compares names, not the letters drawn; an @font-face rule that gives a Vision typeface’s name to a font installed on the machine is a deviation.

measured.title: Corner radii: every drawn box uses a radius of the Vision
measured.note: Boxes with a fill, an edge, or a picture are compared; a radius of 0 is always allowed.

measured.title: Contrast: required by Floor A1 of the Vision
measured.note: The ratio of each text to its background by the WCAG 2.x formula. The Vision writes Floor A1, so a ratio below its least is a deviation. 27 text readings (one for each text and window width) could not be measured: 27 because the text or a box around it is drawn partly transparent.
measured.informationHead: Texts whose contrast the program could not read. A person must judge these by eye:

measured.title: Content: the three required texts of the Brief are where a person can read them
measured.note: The business name, the headline, and the primary action, as the Mockup shows them, compared without regard to letter case or runs of white space, in each reading on its own. A text counts only where it is drawn at 6 pixels or more, not nearly transparent, in a color that is not transparent, and inside the window; a text under a clip-path or a mask is not measured.

measured.title: Width: the page is not wider than its window
measured.note: Measured in each reading; sideways scrolling, and text cut off at the window’s edge where a person cannot reach it, are deviations.

measured.title: Floors: the part of each requirement that a program can check
measured.note: The Vision’s section 7 writes 48 requirements in an edition without a number (an older Vision) of the Floors; this program reads edition 2, and the two may word a requirement differently. The program checked none of them. Write the Vision again from the Studio, then check again.
measured.informationHead: What the program checked of each requirement, and no more than this:

stillNeedsPerson: What the page looks like. The program measured colors, typefaces, corner radii, contrast, and widths; it did not look at the page.
Whether the page works with the keyboard alone, and with a screen reader.
Whether the words are right and say what the owner means.
Every craft rule of the Vision. The check of each rule searches a style sheet for the Mockup’s own marks, so it cannot judge the style sheet of another page.
The states that the program did not open: hover, focus, open menus, and every page other than the one given.
Shadows, gradients, and images. The program did not compare them with the Vision.
All other window widths. The program read the page at 375, 768, and 1280 pixels only, each with motion allowed and with reduced motion; a page can show another design at any other width.

A page that recognizes the check. The program reads the page as a visitor’s browser would, when it has loaded and again two seconds later, but a page can still find signs of the check and show it another design.
Whether the typefaces drawn are the Vision’s. The site’s font files are not there during the check, so the program compares the names that the page gives its typefaces, not the letters that it draws.
Dark mode, touch screens, and other window heights. The program reads the page in light mode, with a mouse, in a window 800 pixels tall; a page can show another design in each.

Other screens and settings. The program reads the page on a screen of ordinary pixel density; a page can show another design on a high-density screen (most phones), in print, with high contrast, or in another language setting.
What happens later. The program stops reading about five seconds after the page has loaded. A page can change after that, or when a person scrolls, clicks, or types.
Frames. The program does not read what an iframe, a frame, an object, or an embed draws; it counts each as not measured.
Closed shadow roots. The program reads the page and every open shadow root; a closed one is out of its reach.
Contrast against what lies under a text on screen. The program reads the color of the boxes that hold a text, so a text placed over another box, or blended with it, can have another contrast.

The Floors of the Vision. The program checked only a part of some requirements (see “Floors” above). It checked nothing of A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S9, S10, S11, H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, Q2, Q3, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13, P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8, P9, P12, P13; the settings of the host (the ids that begin with H) are made at the host and cannot be read from a page.
